Hi [name],

Thank you for your email.

I've reviewed your complaint about the presentation of the Full-Time Result market for the Spain vs Argentina World Cup Final and the settlement of your bets on it.

You note that the Full-Time Result market is settled after 90 minutes. That's correct, and it's the market you selected. Rule 12.1 of our football betting rules states: "Football markets apply to the standard length of 90 minutes including stoppage/injury time unless stated otherwise. Markets for standard 90-minute games do not take extra-time or penalty shootouts into account." This is the default for every football match market we offer, including a World Cup Final.

The market you selected was presented as a three-way market: Spain, Draw, Argentina. The Draw option is the key distinction. A market for the overall winner of a knockout match would have no draw selection, because extra time and penalties always produce a winner. The Draw exists precisely because this market settles at the end of regular time, where a level score is a possible outcome. The three selections identify the market type.

We also offer a separate "To advance" market on knockout fixtures, covered by Rule 12.5.20, which states: "For tournaments featuring single-elimination and similar formats, this market will be settled on a match's final result, including extra time or penalties." That's the market for the overall match winner, and it's a different market from the one you selected.

On your point that a World Cup Final cannot end after 90 minutes: the match goes to extra time if the scores are level, but the result at 90 minutes is still a real, settled outcome. That's what the Full-Time Result market settles on.

On presentation: our general betting rules, Rule 2.1, state that "It is the customer's responsibility to have read and accepted Smarkets Betting Rules prior to placing any bet, and be fully aware of any specific rules affecting any market they wish to bet on." Our Terms and Conditions likewise say that before placing a bet you should make yourself aware of both the general betting rules and the sport-specific rules for the relevant market.

The market was presented and settled in line with our published rules, and we've noted your comments on the presentation. Goodwill adjustments are made where something went wrong on our side, and nothing in this case gives grounds for one. The settlement of your bets stands.

As this is our final response to your complaint, you may refer the matter to your independent dispute resolution provider. If you're in the UK, you can contact IBAS (Independent Betting Adjudication Service); an adjudication form must be requested in the first instance.

IBAS
PO Box 62639
London
EC3P 3AS
Email: adjudication@ibas-uk.co.uk

If you're outside the UK, you can raise a dispute with eCOGRA at ecogra.org/ata/policies_procedures.php

Kind regards,
[name]
Smarkets Support
issues: Complaint process: this is a formal complaint under T&Cs 16.1 (email to support, escalated to management, outcome endeavoured within 10 days of receipt; the Making a complaint help page allows up to 8 weeks in some circumstances). It should be logged as a complaint and sent within SLA. The customer's explicit request for a final response means this reply is the final position and the ADR block (T&Cs 16.2 IBAS / 16.3 eCOGRA) is appropriate; per 16.2 an adjudication form must be requested in the first instance.

Jurisdiction: the customer's country is unknown from the complaint. The draft bifurcates the ADR pointer (IBAS UK / eCOGRA non-UK). Confirm jurisdiction before sending; T&Cs 16.4 (MGA) and 16.5 (EU ODR) also exist but we recommend not over-offering routes.

'No system error occurred' must NOT be stated: the council-verified reference flags this as unverifiable from docs alone. The draft instead says 'presented and settled in line with our published rules', which is the supported claim.

Do not invent account or bet facts: the draft contains no bet IDs, stakes, or dates. Before sending, verify the actual settlement outcome (the bet settled on the 90-minute result, i.e. Draw/Spain/Argentina per the real result) against account data, and verify the market name shown to the customer.

Rule quotes verified character-exact against ~/smarkets-api-support/: Rule 12.1 (90-minute default), Rule 12.5.1 (full-time result), Rule 12.5.20 (To advance settles on final result incl. extra time/pens), Rule 2.1 (customer responsibility), T&Cs Section 6 intro and 16.1-16.3.

Goodwill request: deny. Goodwill adjustments are for when something went wrong on our side; the market was correctly presented and settled. The council-verified pattern is that the customer's own logic is self-defeating (if a Final cannot end at 90 minutes, why would a Draw selection exist?) - argued implicitly via the Draw pillar, not stated as a gotcha.
